title: Introduction to Expo Router
overview: Expo Router is a file-based routing system for Expo applications that simplifies navigation by creating routes from files and folders.

example.title: File Based Routing
example.content:
app/
 ├── index.tsx
 ├── profile.tsx
 └── settings.tsx

Each file becomes a route.

title: File Based Navigation
overview: Expo Router automatically creates navigation routes based on the file structure inside the app directory.

title: Stack Navigation
overview: Stack navigation displays screens on top of each other and provides back navigation between screens.

example.title: Stack Example
example.content:
Home Screen
 ↓
Details Screen
 ↓
Profile Screen

title: Tabs Navigation
overview: Tabs navigation allows users to switch between major sections of an application using a tab bar.

title: Dynamic Routes
overview: Dynamic routes allow screens to receive changing values such as IDs or parameters from the URL.

title: Navigation Methods
overview: Expo Router provides methods to move between screens, replace routes, and go back.

title: Route Groups
overview: Route groups organize screens without affecting the actual URL structure.

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned Expo Router basics including file-based routing, stacks, tabs, dynamic routes, and navigation methods.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ Files create routes.
✔ Stack manages screen flow.
✔ Tabs manage sections.
✔ Dynamic routes handle parameters.
